name: @forguncy-react-workspace/runtime
//: `src/` imports `@forguncy-react-workspace/core/browser`, never bare `core`. That is not a
style choice: bare `core` re-exports `cell-registry` and `config-loader`, which read the
project off disk, so importing any name from it evaluates `node:fs`/`node:path`/`node:crypto`
at module scope. This package is the façade that Cell source calls (#27), so it has to be
loadable in a browser and flattenable into a Cell artifact — and with the bare import it was
neither: Vite's browser-external stub threw during module init, and `compileCell` refused the
artifact with four `unresolved-dependency-decision` diagnostics for `node:*`.
A reviewer tempted to collapse the two back into one should read `core`'s `src/browser.ts`
first: `browser.test.ts` asserts the projection's module list and its `node:`-free graph,
which is what keeps this claim from being a comment.
`./cell` is the production Cell entry (#124): `cell-runtime.ts` re-exported alone, reaching
`provider.ts`, `host-provider.ts`, `port.ts` and `core/cell-props` — never `local-dev.ts`,
`mock-provider.ts`, `cell-fixture.ts` or the capability registry. The compiler's generated
binding imports this subpath (its resolved id is embedded in the binding source), so a Cell
artifact carries the runtime and none of the toolchain. `.` remains the whole package, with
the same exports it had before, because `dev-harness`, `examples/runtime-facade` and the
tests read the contracts from there.
`sideEffects: false` is a declaration, not a hope: no module in either package does work at
import time besides building its own constants. `provider.ts`'s one `let` is a slot that
starts `undefined` and is only written by `installRuntimeFacadeProvider`; `capabilities.ts`
builds its derived channel lists from `core` records, which is pure computation over data
this package already imports. Nothing registers a global, patches a prototype or reads the
environment.
